account: Pregão 15/2021 of the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, a glove tender estimated at R$34 million, reused the price survey of Pregão 05/2021. On the recommendation of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), it was suspended and re-estimated, which cut R$2,381,663.00. The auction held on 21 July 2021 bought every item at or below the new estimates, for a total of R$14,315,793.42. In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil, with accuracy that fell from 88.27% in testing to 73.91% in later auditing. She did not examine these tenders. A CGU statement of 4 October 2023 describes five preventive audits of tenders by federal hospitals and institutes in Rio de Janeiro, among them the Ipanema tender. The automated tool ALICE supported them. The CGU says that this prevented at least R$8.33 million of overpriced purchases. At the Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), a glove auction estimated at R$11 million was re-estimated at R$5.1 million after ALICE indicated prices above market. That avoided about R$5.95 million. The statement gives no date or tender number for the INCA auction.

ai_role.statement: The CGU states the audits were done “com apoio da ferramenta automatizada ALICE”. At INCA, it says, the overpricing risk was identified “com a ajuda do ALICE”. For the Ipanema tender, suspension followed a CGU recommendation after analysis of the price survey. ALICE's documented role is alerting and supporting the audit; auditors and managers decided. Developer and deployer are the same public body. The CGU page is on record as an archived copy, because the live page was restricted during Brazil's 2026 electoral period.

comparator.quote: Observou-se, no entanto, que foi utilizada a mesma pesquisa de preço do pregão de n. º 05/2021 e por recomendação da CGU, o certame foi suspenso e uma nova estimativa de preços foi realizada. A nova análise reduziu o valor total do pregão em R$ 2.381.663,00. Em 21 de julho de 2021, o pregão foi realizado e todos os itens foram adquiridos por valores unitários iguais ou inferiores aos estimados pela unidade, totalizando o montante de R$ 14.315.793,42.

fields.account: Pregão 15/2021 of the Hospital Federal de Ipanema, a glove tender estimated at R$34 million, reused the price survey of Pregão 05/2021. On the recommendation of the Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU), it was suspended and re-estimated, which cut R$2,381,663.00. The auction held on 21 July 2021 bought every item at or below the new estimates, for a total of R$14,315,793.42. In March 2023 Fernanda Odilla of the University of Bologna reported in an independent study that Alice has helped auditors stop irregular tenders across Brazil, with accuracy that fell from 88.27% in testing to 73.91% in later auditing. She did not examine these tenders. A CGU statement of 4 October 2023 describes five preventive audits of tenders by federal hospitals and institutes in Rio de Janeiro, among them the Ipanema tender. The automated tool ALICE supported them. The CGU says that this prevented at least R$8.33 million of overpriced purchases. At the Instituto Nacional de Câncer (INCA), a glove auction estimated at R$11 million was re-estimated at R$5.1 million after ALICE indicated prices above market. That avoided about R$5.95 million. The statement gives no date or tender number for the INCA auction.

purpose: Preventive audit of federal procurement notices using automated risk alerts to stop overpriced purchases before award

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary is identified. Patients benefit only indirectly, through preserved hospital budgets.

The result mattered to the hospitals and to the federal budget. The audits cut R$2,381,663.00 from one auction and about R$5.95 million from another. The CGU reports that the five audits avoided R$8.33 million.
The effect is small at national scale, where federal purchasing is about R$119 billion a year.
